content: 1. Upon arrival at the healthcare facility, the woman is registered, and her administrative and demographic information is recorded. This step may not be necessary for every visit if the woman is already being followed by the same healthcare worker or receiving services in a community setting. 2. A rapid assessment and management (RAM) process is conducted by the registration clerk or the first healthcare worker the woman encounters. This involves checking for any visible danger signs that may require immediate attention. 3. If danger signs are identified, the healthcare worker determines whether the woman needs an urgent referral. If so, she is referred immediately based on the findings and directed to the appropriate antenatal care (ANC) referral process. 4. Pregnancy is confirmed using a urine dipstick test or a blood test. 5. The healthcare worker determines whether this is the woman’s first ANC contact or a follow-up visit. 6. A quick check is performed to assess for any danger signs that may require in-facility management or referral. If no danger signs are present, routine ANC care proceeds. 7. If it is the woman’s first ANC contact, the healthcare worker collects detailed information about her current pregnancy, past medical and obstetric history, medications, behaviors, immunization status, and other relevant background information. 8. The healthcare worker follows up on any previously reported symptoms, behaviors, or medications. 9. A physical examination is conducted, including measurements of weight and height (if it is the first contact), maternal examination, and fetal assessment. 10. Laboratory tests and imaging, such as ultrasounds, are ordered or followed up on as necessary. The healthcare worker explains the purpose of these tests to the woman. 11. Based on the findings, the healthcare worker provides counseling on potential risks, behaviors, and diagnoses. Preventive services and treatments that can be provided at the facility are administered, including admission to another part of the facility if required. 12. If a referral is needed, the healthcare worker arranges for the woman to be referred to a higher-level facility or provider. This may include psychosocial, emotional, cultural, or social support services, such as counseling, peer-support organizations, or financial and nutritional assistance. 13. If no referral is required, the healthcare worker schedules a follow-up contact. 14. The woman is advised on self-care interventions at home or in the community, including monitoring her pregnancy and managing physiological symptoms. She is also informed about when to contact a healthcare worker or facility if danger signs arise or if self-management is not effective. 15. If the woman returns for follow-up services, the process continues until delivery or as needed. 16. In emergency situations, immediate referral is prioritized, bypassing standard steps. The woman is stabilized and given pre-referral treatment if necessary. Emergency transport is organized, and the referral facility is contacted to ensure readiness to receive the woman. 17. The referral process includes identifying and discussing referral location options with the woman and her family, ensuring the referral facility can accommodate her needs, and providing all necessary clinical and demographic information to the receiving facility. 18. Community health workers (CHWs) provide routine outreach services, including home visits or community day interactions. They assess for danger signs, provide counseling, and offer support for healthy behaviors and symptom management. 19. CHWs also schedule follow-up contacts and remind the woman of danger signs and emergency transport options. They encourage self-monitoring and self-management of symptoms, with instructions to contact healthcare providers if issues persist. 20. Data reporting involves reviewing the accuracy, validity, and completeness of data, correcting any quality issues, generating aggregate reports, and submitting them electronically. Supervisors review and provide feedback as needed to ensure data quality and compliance with reporting requirements.
